scope.summary: Implement the explicit coupling-link graph per Section 13.17 (BK-17.1, TAI-BK-036), closing REQ-003 and OBR architecture implication 1: CouplingLink {link_id, source_channel_key, target_channel_key, piecewise-linear curve, enabled} stored in BodySpec.coupling_links — named, inspectable, per-edge disableable, deletable, with an isolate-region override suspending all inbound links for a region during authoring. Links write TARGET CHANNEL VALUES only; they never write vertices, never bypass masks, and hidden drivers of any kind are a Blocking defect (anti-ERC).
acceptance_criteria: CouplingLink type matches TAI-BK-036: link_id unique within the body, source/target channel keys validated against the registry, curve as Vec<[f32; 2]> piecewise-linear pairs, enabled flag for per-edge disable without deletion.

Link resolution runs at channel-write time in the kernel: setting a source channel propagates curve-mapped values to target channels as ordinary channel edits (each emitting TailorBodyChannelChanged with actor attribution) — resolution never touches solver vertex data.
Cycles are rejected at link insert (typed error naming the cycle path); self-links are rejected.
isolate_region(body_id, group_key) suspends all inbound links targeting channels of that group until released; suspended links are visible as suspended, not deleted.
list_links(body_id) returns the full graph for inspector surfaces; there is no other cross-channel propagation mechanism in the codebase (module doc + negative test assert this).
scope.risk_if_missed: Daz's ERC freeze creates invisible, error-prone couplings users cannot audit or remove; if BodyKit's only correlation mechanism is not this inspectable graph, hidden links accumulate and the decoupling law dies in practice while passing BODY_DECOUPLE_VALID on paper.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend/solver scope: behavior is observable via TraceProjection, typed TAILOR_BODY_* receipts, and the 13.12 capture APIs; operator/model GUI exposure rides the BodyKit panes (13.27) and is validated there.

target_entries: Tailor UserManual > BodyKit shape channels and measurements

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: This MT owns authoritative, job, or external-tool lifecycle events and must project the same event_id, run_id, actor_id, and correlation_id from EventLedger into Flight Recorder.
This MT emits typed diagnostics through its owning command or job and inherits retention, health, and projection behavior from the shared diagnostics substrate.
The owning native shell or scheduled job supplies Palmistry coverage; this MT must preserve operation identity and recovery handles.

risks: Broad MT scope can hide multiple review targets.
Markdown MT lists may disagree with packet-declared active/next MT truth.
Receipt routing may target an old MT if contract identity is omitted.
minimum_controls: Exactly one primary proof target per MT unless the packet records why not.
MT identity must be stable and referenced by receipt correlation.
Generated projection drift must not wake Coder or Validator by itself.

required_changes_before_execution: Separate control independence from declared feathered deformation support, skeletal propagation, physical response, and explicit coupling.
Consume the signed technical refinement, canonical command/surface registries, classified HBR tiers, and task-oriented UserManual contract before execution.
